title: Prompt Caching: When It Lowers Your AI API Bill
description: Calculate cache savings from measured hit rates, provider-specific rates and repeated prompt prefixes.
tldr: Prompt caching can reduce the price of eligible repeated input, but savings depend on cache hits, minimum lengths, expiration rules and provider rates. Measure cached tokens in usage records before claiming a percentage.

sections.heading: What gets cached
sections.body: Providers can reuse processing for eligible repeated prompt content, often a stable prefix such as a system prompt, tool definitions or a document. Cache behavior differs by API. OpenAI documents automatic caching for eligible prompts; Anthropic documents explicit cache controls and separate write/read charges. Read the rules for the exact model and endpoint.

sections.heading: Calculate the effective rate
sections.body: Let an input segment contain N tokens. If its normal rate is R and a cache hit rate is H with cached-read rate C, the simple expected cost is N × ((1 − H)R + HC) / 1,000,000. If cache writes have a premium, add that cost. The formula shows why a large advertised discount does not equal the same reduction in the whole bill: output and uncached input still cost money.

sections.heading: A worked illustration
sections.body: Suppose a repeated 10,000-token prefix has a $3 standard input rate, a $0.30 cached-read rate and an 80% cache hit rate. Per request, expected prefix cost is 10,000 × (0.2 × 3 + 0.8 × 0.30) / 1,000,000 = $0.0084, versus $0.03 without caching. That is 72% less for this prefix alone, before cache writes and output. The rates are illustrative.

sections.heading: Measure in production
sections.body: Log cache creation and read tokens from usage records. Keep the repeated prefix stable and place changing user data later where the API's rules allow. Review expiration, minimum cacheable length and provider-specific retention terms. Compare total invoice before and after, not only one line item.

faq.question: Does caching cut my entire API bill by 90%?
faq.answer: No fixed discount applies to every bill. Savings affect eligible input and depend on hit rate, write/read prices and the share of output or other services.

ctaText: Estimate your own usage with TokenRate tools, then compare with the provider's billing page.
